title: Clean Engineering, Unstable Measurement: A Preregistered Reliability Failure of Black-Box LLM Observers on Shared Endpoints
why_read: A rigorous, preregistered empirical study showing that LLM-as-judge evaluation pipelines are far less reliable and reproducible than commonly assumed, with real implications for anyone gating decisions on LLM judges.
analysis: The authors ran large-scale preregistered audits (nearly 53,000 requests) testing whether repeated or byte-identical queries to the same hosted LLM endpoint yield consistent judge rankings, finding dramatic instability (Spearman ~0.4-0.78 versus required ~0.9-0.99) even accounting for provider switching or self-hosting. This is a substantive methodological critique with concrete numbers and actionable design rules, directly relevant to teams using LLM judges for evals, leaderboards, or RLHF-style gating. It's a rare piece of rigorous measurement science applied to a widely-assumed-stable AI infrastructure component.
